sections.h2: Which Ellis County office holds the deed records?
sections.html:
The County Clerk records real property instruments, and the office sits on the second floor of 109 S. Jackson St. in Waxahachie, while mail goes to P.O. Box 250, Waxahachie 75168. The property recording line is 972-825-5070, fax 972-825-5075, and the counter serves the public on weekdays between eight in the morning and four-thirty in the afternoon.

Anything that touches title lands in this office: every flavor of deed, plus leases, sale contracts and powers of attorney tied to local land.

Besides deeds, the same office files birth, death, marriage and military discharge records, handles probate and guardianship filings and serves as clerk of the Commissioners Court. Birth records go back to 1850. Passports, divorces and felony matters belong to the District Clerk instead.

One limit is worth knowing: clerks may not give legal advice or prepare an instrument for you, citing Government Code Sec. 81.101. Arrive with a finished document that shows a return address, or let a title company file it.

The Recording Division page offers eRecording through approved vendors, and the county links a public records search. Filing electronically avoids a drive to Waxahachie.

sections.h2: What does the Ellis County recording schedule cost?
sections.html:
Since January 1, 2024 the first page of a recorded document is $25.00 and each added page, part of a page or rider is $4.00. The clerk's page explains that Senate Bill 1612 repealed the separate $1.00 document filing fee, which is why the first-page charge dropped to that level.

sections.h2: How do payments and copies work at the clerk's counter?
sections.html:
Checks go to the Ellis County Clerk. Cards and debit are accepted with a processing charge of 2.4 percent or $1, whichever is larger. A returned check costs $25.00, a check older than 90 days is refused, and refunds wait for the check to clear.

  • Noncertified paper copy or paper-to-electronic conversion: $1.00 per page or part of a page.
  • Electronic copy of an electronic document: $1.00 up to 10 pages, then $0.10 for each added page.
  • Certification: $5.00. Full-size plat copy: $10.00.

Copy rates cite Local Government Code Sec. 118.0145, and the certification fee cites Sec. 118.014.

sections.h2: How big is Ellis County and who lives there?
sections.html:
By QuickFacts, 240,867 people lived here in mid-2025 across 935.75 land square miles, up 25.2 percent since 2020. The two prior headcounts were 192,455 and 149,610, taken in 2020 and 2010.

Ellis County's welcome page lists 952 square miles in all and describes 15 cities, 7 towns and unincorporated communities including Avalon, Forreston and Telico. Its city list takes in Cedar Hill, Ennis, Ferris, Garrett, Glenn Heights, Grand Prairie, Italy, Mansfield, Maypearl, Midlothian, Milford, Oak Leaf, Ovilla, Palmer, Pecan Hill, Red Oak, Venus and Waxahachie.

  • Median household income, 2020 to 2024: $99,595
  • Mean commute: 30.3 minutes each way
  • People 65 or older: 14.1 percent; veterans: 10,529
  • Share of residents still at the same address after twelve months: 88.6 percent
  • Households with a broadband subscription: 92.5 percent

Numbers like a half-hour commute and a six-figure household income describe a county where many owners work elsewhere in the Dallas area and live here for space.

sections.h2: Why is the Waxahachie courthouse relevant to a property owner?
sections.html:
It is the county seat's landmark and a useful sign of how long records here run. Texas lawmakers carved the county out of Navarro County on December 20, 1849, and voters were told to name the seat Waxahachie, which the county says comes from a Tejas word for buffalo creek. The 62 acres for the seat along Waxahachie Creek were donated by an early settler.

The present courthouse is the fourth on the site and was accepted in 1897. It is nine stories with an 800-pound bell in the clock tower, and it anchors a National Register district with 42 more contributing buildings around the square. A restoration that ran roughly from 1999 to the early 2000s was helped by a state matching grant of $3,567,787.

The courthouse history lists an 1850 log cabin costing $59, a frame building in 1854 and a limestone courthouse around 1870 before the 1897 building. Ask your title company to trace older deeds back that far if a description looks unusual.

sections.h2: Who appraises Ellis County property and where do I pay?
sections.html:
The Ellis Appraisal District sets value, and the Ellis County Tax Office at 302 N. Monroe St., Waxahachie, phone 972-825-5150, can give contact details for each taxing unit. Parcel data is maintained by the appraisal district, and the county points to ECAD for ownership and parcel downloads.

The appraisal district offers an online portal for property alerts, plus pages for filing a protest and booking an informal appointment. A tax transparency site lists proposed rates from each unit in late summer. Rates are adopted by the taxing units, not by the appraisal district, a point the district's own message stresses: value and rate together make the bill.

The state levies no property tax of its own. Value is measured every January 1, notices reach homesteads first in spring, protests close in mid-May and bills arrive in the fall.

sections.h2: What does a title search turn up in Ellis County?
sections.html:
• Vesting deed. The grantee on the last recorded deed should be the seller.
  • Lien releases. A paid mortgage can linger in the index until a release is filed.
  • Tax liens. Federal and state liens are recorded by the clerk under the fees above.
  • Heirs. A property passed by death may need an executor's deed, a death-transfer deed, a muniment order or an affidavit of heirship, depending on how the estate was handled.

Recording needs a signature plus a notary-style acknowledgment or two witnesses. After a death the clerk cannot amend the earlier deed to list heirs; a new instrument must carry them.

Ellis County is served by Avalon, Ennis, Ferris, Italy, Maypearl, Midlothian, Milford, Palmer, Red Oak and Waxahachie school districts, according to the county's links. Which district a house sits in affects the school tax portion of the bill, so confirm it on the appraisal district's parcel page.

sections.h2: What homestead protections matter when selling?
sections.html:
Buyers closing in spring or summer should ask the appraisal district about claiming a homestead right away, because an exemption can start mid-year when the seller never held one. School districts exempt $140,000 of a residence's value, and seniors and disabled owners get another $60,000 plus a school tax ceiling.

Appraised value of a homestead may rise only 10 percent a year once the exemption has been in place a full year. Heirs missing from the recorded deed must give the district an affidavit, the death certificate and a recent utility bill.

faqs.q: Which office files a deed for an Ellis County house?
faqs.a: Record it with the County Clerk at 109 S. Jackson St., 2nd Floor, Waxahachie, or send it through an approved eRecording vendor. The property recording line is 972-825-5070.

faqs.q: What will recording a deed cost in Ellis County?
faqs.a: Page one is $25.00 and each later page, partial page or rider adds $4.00 in the 2024 schedule. Every name past five adds a quarter.

faqs.q: Can the Ellis County Clerk prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. The clerk's page cites Government Code Sec. 81.101: staff may not advise on law or draft an instrument, so hire a lawyer or a title firm to write it.

faqs.q: What are the Ellis County Clerk's hours?
faqs.a: It opens Monday to Friday, eight to four-thirty. County offices also close on observed holidays; the county's site announced a Veterans Day closure on November 11, 2026.

faqs.q: Which Ellis County office mails a tax statement?
faqs.a: Statements come out of the county tax office on behalf of the taxing units, and the appraisal district does not bill. The Ellis County Tax Office is at 302 N. Monroe St., Waxahachie, phone 972-825-5150.
